scope: Assess T3 Code extensibility and suitability as an execution base for omniagent-plus; no implementation, migration, live-provider invocation, or roadmap change.

conclusion.recommendation: Prioritize a bounded T3 adapter and server-admission feasibility spike before investing further in Omnigent-specific WIRE/INTEG work. Keep Omnigent operational until the spike passes.
conclusion.qualified_answer: T3 development main is a credible better execution and operator platform for this project's solo multi-host coding workflow. It is not clearly a better general extension framework: native drivers are build-time registrations and universal custom policy needs server integration.

confidence.extension_seams: High: inspected documentation, registry, native interface, ACP configuration, external MCP tools, and runtime composition.
confidence.migration_cost: Medium: mapped current public contracts and safety boundaries; no T3 adapter implemented.
confidence.live_provider_parity: Unproven: replay tests pass, but no live Opus TUI, Gemini CLI, or cross-host integrated launch was exercised.

snapshots.note: The inspected provider-core packages, ACP registry configuration, external orchestration MCP tools, and V2 durable effect outbox are development-main findings. They are not the stable v0.0.45 architecture, and the nightly has not been asserted identical to the pinned main.
Policy modules, headless harness plugin registry and typed Python client verified in the stable tag, not only main.

extension_paths.name: T3 external bridge
extension_paths.interface: OAuth-authenticated HTTP MCP for orchestration and typed authenticated WebSocket RPC; HTTP orchestration snapshots/history are read routes.
extension_paths.benefit: Reuse T3 execution and UI without initially forking.
constraints: New outside-agent OAuth enrollment requires operator approval.
RPC contracts and client packages are internal workspace code, not a independently versioned public SDK.
Only requests sent through the bridge are governed by its policy. This boundary limitation also applies to an external wrapper around Omnigent.

extension_paths.name: T3 local ACP command
extension_paths.interface: Configurable executable, literal arguments and environment settings; generic ACP protocol adapter.
extension_paths.benefit: Add an ACP-speaking agent without a custom native driver or rebuilding T3.
constraints: An arbitrary TUI or phase-loop CLI entrypoint is not an ACP server.
ACP does not provide portable native subagent lineage or account isolation.
Generic rollback may start a fresh native session; permission enforcement depends on the agent.
Bridge capabilities must be reported truthfully and backed by replay fixtures.

extension_paths.name: T3 native driver
extension_paths.interface: ProviderAdapterV2 and ProviderDriver with ProviderHost infrastructure; packages/provider-<name> server/client/settings/testing exports.
extension_paths.benefit: Rich native session, turn, steering, interruption, fork/rollback, background work and lifecycle integration.
constraints: Static server and client registrations require a source build.
provider-core is private workspace code; there is no demonstrated stable third-party native plugin loader.
Fast-moving V2 requires pinned versions and contract/replay compatibility checks.

extension_paths.name: T3 admission service
extension_paths.interface: New service integrated into shared launch/command paths and rechecked immediately before provider-side execution, using Effect service composition.
extension_paths.benefit: Possible common enforcement across UI, MCP, scheduled jobs, delegation and recovery.
constraints: This is an architectural proposal, not an existing configurable policy hook.
Requires a maintained server fork or an upstream-supported seam.
An early launch check alone cannot authorize a queued effect indefinitely; lease/identity/cooldown need a dispatch-time recheck.
Session opening can trigger hooks/processes; gating only startTurn may be too late.
Native autonomous child work and per-tool filesystem fencing require an explicitly defined enforcement scope.

extension_paths.name: Omnigent installed extensions
extension_paths.interface: Python entry points for community headless harnesses and sandbox providers; custom function policies via server/agent/session configuration; typed HTTP/SSE SDK.
extension_paths.benefit: More operator-configurable backend extension and policy mechanisms already in stable v0.17.0.
constraints: Community native TUI harness metadata is explicitly rejected by the loader.
Not every native provider execution path should be assumed governed by a mediated-tool policy without coverage proof.
Browser extensions primarily supply pages/navigation, not arbitrary server plugins.

runtime_findings.finding: V2 commits command receipt, events, projections and outbox effects transactionally before publishing.
runtime_findings.implication: Good foundation for durable orchestration; an accepted command is not completed execution.

runtime_findings.finding: Process-loss recovery cancels process-bound pending/running effects and requeues explicitly replay-safe running effects.
runtime_findings.implication: Avoids blind mutation replay; does not prove exactly-once native execution across every crash boundary.

runtime_findings.finding: Persisted usage-limit recovery already handles reset time, snooze, idempotent commands and optional automatic resumption.
runtime_findings.implication: Quota recovery alone is not a strong unique feature of omniagent-plus.

runtime_findings.finding: Each T3 environment owns its execution/state; repository correlation explicitly does not route work between environments.
runtime_findings.implication: Remote connectivity is not a global cross-host scheduler.

runtime_findings.finding: workspaceLease is a per-process semaphore map, and V2 outbox leases are local execution claims.
runtime_findings.implication: Neither replaces our fleet holder/fence/expiry contract.

runtime_findings.finding: Portable handoffs summarize content with whitespace normalization and 240-character text prefixes.
runtime_findings.implication: Provider switching does not imply lossless native memory migration.

runtime_findings.finding: T3 built-in Claude integration uses claude-agent-sdk.query.
runtime_findings.implication: It does not automatically replace our exact manual Opus TUI review leg.

retain: Fleet lease contracts and holder/fence enforcement
Routing, identity and provider-family cooldown decisions
State ledger for policy and review evidence
Independent panel/merge gate and manual review-leg requirements
required_contract_changes: Add T3 runtime/backend IDs with schema compatibility tests; current runtimeIds accepts only omnigent.
Make agent specifications an explicit backend-discriminated contract; current type is OmnigentAgentSpecRef.
Map neutral sessions/turn handles to environment/project/thread/app run and provider instance; an app run may span native turns.
Map stream snapshots/cursors, changed nodes and native IDs to neutral events without duplicate terminal settlement.
Treat interrupt acknowledgment separately from observed terminal cancellation.
Apply DATA content controls to projected evidence; do not copy raw full-content T3 history into a metadata-only ledger.
carryover_and_mapping.ownership_proposal: T3 owns provider execution and provider conversation history. Consiliency coordination owns routing/lease authority and approval/evidence records. Avoid two independently authoritative execution logs.
carryover_and_mapping.roadmap_status: DATA and COORD accepted on main; WIRE and INTEG are not accepted there. Existing unmerged WIRE branch preserved.

proposed_spike_acceptance: Drive one real provider through create/send/stream/history/resume/interrupt and prove environment, provider instance and identity mapping.
Inject duplicate commands and restart around acceptance/provider-start/result boundaries; preserve command identity and terminal uniqueness without blind prompt replay.
Race two hosts for one fleet resource; expired or stale holders and unreachable lease authority must fail closed before new provider work.
Exercise UI, external MCP, delegation, scheduled/recovery and native continuation paths against the same admission decision, or document a deliberately narrower owned-call boundary.
Demonstrate actual required manual Opus TUI and Gemini workflow, preserving subscription authentication and tool use.
Verify metadata-only exports, bounded history/replay and truthful fork/rollback/background capabilities.
Rebase the integration across a T3 update and measure changed registrations/contracts; reject a design that requires broad orchestrator or client rewrites.
